Consider the comparison morphism <MATH_0001>.
Let <MATH_0002> denote the class of proper morphisms.
For <MATH_0003> in <MATH_0004> denote
<MATH_0005>
the full subcategory consisting of sheaves of the form
<MATH_0006> where <MATH_0007> is a
torsion abelian sheaf on <MATH_0008>
Then Cohomology on Sites, Properties
(<REF_0001>),
(<REF_0002>),
(<REF_0003>),
(<REF_0004>), and
(<REF_0005>)
of Cohomology on Sites, Situation
<REF_0006> hold.

We first show that <MATH_0001>
is a weak Serre subcategory by checking conditions (1), (2), (3), and (4)
of Homology, Lemma <REF_0001>.
Parts (1), (2), (3) are immediate as <MATH_0002> is exact and
fully faithful for example by Lemma <REF_0002>. If
<MATH_0003>
is a short exact sequence in <MATH_0004>
then <MATH_0005>
is exact by Lemma <REF_0003>.
In particular we see that <MATH_0006> is an abelian
torsion sheaf on <MATH_0007>.
Hence <MATH_0008> is in
<MATH_0009> which checks the final condition.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0004>) holds
by the existence of fibre products of schemes,
the fact that the base change of a proper morphism of
schemes is a proper morphism of schemes, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0005>, and
the fact that the base change of a morphism of finite presentation
is a morphism of finite presentation, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0006>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0007>)
follows from the commutative diagram (3) in
Topologies, Lemma <REF_0008>.

<STRUCT_0005><STRUCT_0006>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0009>) is
Lemma <REF_0010>.

<STRUCT_0007><STRUCT_0008>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0011>) holds by
Lemma <REF_0012> part (2)
and the fact that <MATH_0010>
is torsion if <MATH_0011> is an abelian torsion
sheaf on <MATH_0012>, see Lemma <REF_0013>.

<STRUCT_0009><STRUCT_0010>
Cohomology on Sites, Property (<REF_0014>)
is implied by More on Morphisms, Lemma
<REF_0015>
combined with the fact that a surjective finite locally free morphism
is surjective, proper, and of finite presentation and hence
defines a h-covering by More on Flatness, Lemma
<REF_0016>.
